results.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in ...
results.content: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) has revolutionised civil engineering, enhancing predictive accuracy, decision-making, and sustainability across domains such as structural health monitoring, geotechnical analysis, transportation systems, water management, and sustainable construction. Previous researches showed that ML and AI techniques can be beneficial in terms of improved cost estimation and budgeting by predicting the future expenses with the help of historical data [23], enhancing risk management during the project lifecycle [24], optimising project’s planning, scheduling, monitoring, and control [25], optimising resource utilisation by predicting their demand [26], predictive analysis in making better and timely decisions, reducing uncertainties and improving project outcomes [27], personnel selection with the focus on hierarchical competency assessment [28], automating repetitive tasks and complex activities to enhance productivity [29], ensuring the safety measures and regulations at construction sites [30], and last but not the least, optimising the quality control by identifying early defects [31].

results.title: Time Series Analysis in Frequency Domain: A Survey of ...
results.content: Time series analysis (Mahalakshmi et al., 2016; Sapankevych and Sankar, 2009; Han et al., 2019) has emerged as the methodological cornerstone supporting data-driven decision-making in domains as diverse like finance (Zhang et al., 2025e; Han et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2025g), urban infrastructure management (Zhang et al., 2025b, 2023a, 2023b, g), and climate system modeling (Bracco et al., 2025). The translation to frequency-domain analysis offers a powerful paradigm shift (Zhou et al., 2022b), transforming the analytical challenge from direct temporal modeling to spectral representation. Our frequency-domain analysis pipeline (Figure 2) establishes a systematic framework comprising four critical stages: data preprocessing (Section 2.4) for signal conditioning, frequency transformation through both traditional spectral methods (Fourier/Wavelet transforms; Section 3) and modern neural approaches (Section 4), rigorous evaluation on standardized benchmarks (Weather in terms of two metrics; Section 5), and practical deployment in domains like healthcare monitoring and financial forecasting (Section 6). A survey on deep learning based time series analysis with frequency transformation.

results.title: Machine learning in peak demand forecasting
results.content: # Machine learning in peak demand forecasting: foundations, trends, and insights. First comprehensive review of peak demand forecasting, analyzing 186 studies. Peak demand forecasting involves predicting the maximum electricity demand within a specific period, which plays a key role in maintaining the efficiency and stability of power systems. The rapid evolution of power systems, driven by advanced metering infrastructure, local energy applications such as electric vehicles, and the increasing adoption of intermittent renewable energy, has introduced greater randomness and reduced predictability in peak demand. Given the pressing need to address more diverse implementation requirements across different contexts, accurate and reliable peak demand forecasting has become increasingly important. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to provide a comprehensive overview of peak demand forecasting methods. Building on this, the study defines a unified framework for peak demand forecasting and offers an in-depth analysis linking these methods to the practical needs of power systems.
